info.name: DIKSHA IAM Orchestration API
info.description: Complete OIDC-based authentication flow with OTP verification, PKCE, and session management

item.name: 01. Flow - Existing User (Web)
item.description: Complete login flow for ACTIVE user via web

request.description: Start login for existing ACTIVE user. Returns status=LOGIN_ALLOWED with authorize redirect URL.
Bridge endpoint that redirects to Keycloak. Returns 302 redirect to Keycloak authorization URL. In manual testing, extract code & state from Keycloak redirect.
Keycloak redirects back with code & state. Orchestrator exchanges code for tokens and sets session cookie. Redirects to original redirectUri.
Retrieve authenticated user profile using session cookie. Returns user info with loginProvider='KEYCLOAK' and org details.

item.name: 02. Flow - First-Time User (Mobile)
item.description: Complete login flow for NEW/first-time user via mobile with OTP

request.description: Start login for NEW/first-time user. Sends OTP and returns status=OTP_SENT with txnId. Mobile channel detected from redirectUri scheme.

exec: console.log('txnId:', b.txnId, '| status:', b.status, '| masked:', b.maskedIdentifier);

request.description: Verify OTP for first-time user. Generates PKCE, nonce, and activation_token. Returns authorize redirect URL.

exec: console.log('OTP verified | txnId:', b.txnId, '| status:', b.status);

request.description: Redirect to Keycloak with activation_token. Keycloak validates activation_token and shows password creation form for first-time users.
Keycloak callback for mobile. Returns sessionCode in redirect instead of setting cookie. Mobile app extracts sessionCode and uses /session/exchange.
Mobile client exchanges sessionCode for access/refresh tokens. sessionCode is single-use. Returns access token, refresh token, and user profile.
Retrieve user profile using Bearer token (from session exchange). Validates token claims and returns user info.

exec: console.log('User from Bearer token:', JSON.stringify(b, null, 2));

request.description: Refresh access token using refresh token. Can be called via explicit refreshToken in body or via session cookie. Returns new access token and optionally new refresh token.
Refresh using session cookie (preferred method for web clients). Automatically uses refresh token from session. Returns new access token and updates cookie TTL.

exec: console.log('No session cookie available (expected if not logged in via web)');

request.description: Revoke refresh token and delete session. For web, also clears session cookie. If logoutAllDevices=true, attempts to revoke all active sessions for user (requires session index).
Should return 400 with error='invalid_client' if clientId is not registered
Should return 400 with error='invalid_request' if redirectUri not allowed for client
Should return 404 with error='user_not_found' if user doesn't exist
Should return 401 with error='invalid_otp' if OTP is incorrect or expired
Should return 400 with error='txn_expired' if transaction is older than 10 minutes
Should return 404 with error='session_code_invalid' if sessionCode doesn't exist or is expired
Should return 400 with error='session_code_used' if sessionCode has already been exchanged (single-use enforcement)

item.name: 07. Flow - SSO Login (Google / State Provider)
item.description: SSO login flow via external identity providers (Google OAuth2 or state-configured OIDC providers). No txnStore/PKCE involved — state is stored directly in stateStore. Session cookie is set on successful callback.

query.description: Optional. Frontend URL to redirect to after successful SSO. Defaults to FRONTEND_REDIRECT_URI env var.

exec: console.log('Expected: State provider not configured -', b.error);

query.description: Authorization code returned by Google. Replace with real code from browser redirect.
Must match the state returned from 7.1. Validated against stateStore.

request.description:
Google redirects here after user authenticates. Orchestrator:
1. Validates state from stateStore (must match provider)
2. Exchanges code for Google ID token
3. Validates ID token claims (issuer, audience, nonce)
4. Resolves/creates user via /users/sso-resolve in iam-service
5. Upserts user in Keycloak
6. Writes mappingStore with activationStatus=ACTIVE
7. Creates session (accessToken/refreshToken stored as null — SSO sessions are cookie-only)
8. Sets HttpOnly session cookie
9. Redirects to redirectUri?sso_success=true&provider=google

NOTE: In real flow the browser follows the redirect from 7.1. This request is for manual inspection only — the simulated code will fail at token exchange with Google.

exec: // In real flow this returns a 302 redirect to the frontend.
// With a simulated/invalid code, Google token exchange will fail → 400.

query.description: Error code returned by provider when user denies access.

request.description: Simulates user denying access on the Google consent screen. Provider sends error=access_denied. Should return 400 with the provider error.

exec: pm.test('error mentions SSO provider error', () => pm.expect(b.error).to.include('SSO provider error'));

query.description: State not present in stateStore (expired or tampered).

request.description: Simulates a callback with an invalid or expired state parameter. stateStore.get() returns null, so the request is rejected. Protects against CSRF attacks.

exec: pm.test('error is Invalid or expired state', () => pm.expect(b.error).to.include('Invalid or expired state'));

query.description: State was generated for 'google' but callback claims 'state_karnataka'. Should be rejected.

request.description: Simulates a provider mismatch attack: using a valid state from a google login to hit the state_karnataka callback. stateStore validates stateData.provider === provider, so this is rejected.

exec: pm.test('error is Invalid or expired state', () => pm.expect(b.error).to.include('Invalid or expired state'));

request.description: Attempts to initiate SSO with a provider not in SUPPORTED_SSO_PROVIDERS. Should return 400.

Retrieve user profile after SSO login using the session cookie set in the callback (step 7.3).

SSO sessions have accessToken/refreshToken=null in the session store — the /me endpoint reads only iamUserId and username from session, so it works correctly for SSO users.

mappingStore returns activationStatus=ACTIVE (set during SSO callback).

Logout for SSO users. No refreshToken is sent in the body (SSO sessions have refreshToken=null). The logout handler:
1. Skips Keycloak token revocation (no refreshToken in body)
2. Deletes the application session from sessionStore
3. Clears the HttpOnly session cookie

This is safe — SSO users have no Keycloak tokens to revoke.

exec: console.log('SSO user logged out at:', b.timestamp);

request.description: Verify orchestrator is running. Returns {ok: true}
